state.issue:
yq: alias sync, anchor marks and the alias redirect apply only to the last document of a multi-document stream

**Severity: Medium** — silent wrong values and dropped anchors in every document but the last of a stream.

## Summary

In a multi-document YAML stream, alias value sync (#711), anchor/alias mark preservation (#763) and the #1351 alias redirect apply only to the **last** document. Every earlier document is written positionally with its `&x`/`*x` marks dropped. Found by the review of PR #2510; reproduces on `main` (`a353c85ba`) before that PR, so it is pre-existing.

## Repro

Verified against Homebrew `yq` v4.53.3:

```console
$ printf 'a: &x {p: 1}\nb: *x\n---\na: &x {p: 3}\nb: *x\n' | yq '.b.p = 9'
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x
---
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x

$ printf 'a: &x {p: 1}\nb: *x\n---\na: &x {p: 3}\nb: *x\n' | succinctly yq '.a.p = 9'   # main
a: {p: 9}
b:
  p: 1
---
a: &x {p: 9}
b: *x
```

Document 0 loses `&x`/`*x` and `b` does not follow the anchor write; document 1 is right. With three documents only the third is right; `--doc 0` reproduces on its own.

## Root cause (not isolated)

Something in the per-document path of `evaluate_yaml_cursor` — `cursor.index().has_aliases()`, `collect_alias_groups(cursor)`, or the comment-tree capture — answers for the whole stream or for the final document rather than the document at hand. `has_aliases()` being an index-wide flag while `collect_alias_groups` walks the per-document cursor is the first thing to check.

## Suggested fix direction

Make the alias-sensitivity gate and the group collection per document (or per document cursor), then add multi-document twins of the existing `#711`/`#763`/`#1351` CLI tests, including `--doc 0`.

## Why this is separate from #1351

#1351 (PR #2510) changes what a write does inside one document; this is about which documents of a stream get that treatment at all, and it predates the PR.
